items.body:
This is an "umbrella" ticket (call it an epic, or whatever) to track the migration of the `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` resource to the [Plugin Framework](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework).

#### Motivation
Check out the [benefits of Plugin Framework](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework-benefits) from HashiCorp. There are quite a lot.

Specific to this provider:

- The Plugin Framework gives [better control](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/framework-benefits#control-over-built-in-behaviors) over `Optional` and `Computed` fields and their *defaults*, which is extremely useful in handling the `clone` operation. During cloning, we inject lots of attributes from a template that are not present in the clone while also overwriting some of the template parameters from the clone.

  Related:
  - #103
  - #247
  - #360
  - #566
  - #718
  - #781 
  - #850
  - #873
  - #1106
  - #1219
  - #1224
  - #1299
  - #1304
  - and others

- Ability to manage data transformations via custom data types (various conventions for lists/sets in the Proxmox API).

- Better support for collection data types (lists, and specifically sets, to handle unordered collections of items).

#### Challenges
- There's a vast amount of functionality to port, and some (or most?) of it needs to be re-implemented to leverage the benefits of the Provider Framework data model/custom types.

- Severe lack of the provider's code test coverage. The changes/re-implementation will introduce new bugs that will be hard to catch.

#### Compatibility
Inevitably, some attribute formats and semantics will be incompatible with the old version. Also, some attributes will be renamed/removed. Known incompatibilities are marked with :exclamation: below.


#### Implementation

The `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm2` resource contains the new implementation.

**Describe the bug**

Using the resource `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` and creating a `user_data` file using `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` resource and using `migrate=true` on the VM when changing the node, the VM is deleted/added instead of changed.

Why I wish to do it this way is to inject per VM specific variables to user_data (cloud-init). Currently I cannot do that if I wish to retain the migrate logic between nodes. Eg `migrate=true`

2. Modify the resource 'vm' to use another host (E.G Migrate the host from one node to another). (Nothing else is changed.)

items.title: vm: importing a VM with its CD-ROM on ide2 leaves `cdrom` out of state
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
When `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` reads a VM, it looks for the CD-ROM only on the `cdrom.interface` already in state. On import there is no state yet, so it falls back to the schema default `ide3`. The Proxmox GUI puts the CD-ROM on `ide2`, so importing such a VM records no `cdrom`, and declaring it afterwards plans to add one.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a VM outside Terraform with `ide2: none,media=cdrom` (the GUI default).
2. Import it: `terraform import proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.example pve/<vmid>`.
3. `terraform state show` lists no `cdrom` (`cdrom.# = 0`).
4. Declare it and plan:

```hcl
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "example" {
  node_name = "pve"
  vm_id     = <vmid>

  cdrom {
    interface = "ide2"
    file_id   = "none"
  }
}
```

The plan shows `+ cdrom { ... }` instead of no change.

**Expected behavior**
An import finds the CD-ROM on whichever interface Proxmox reports it (any `ideN`/`sataN`/`scsiN` with `media=cdrom`) and records it, so declaring the existing drive plans no change and `-generate-config-out` includes it.

**Additional context**
- Found while working on #3229 (same class of import gap for `tpm_state`/`efi_disk`); reproduced on PVE 9.2 with a throwaway acceptance probe.
- Related: #2285 (disks of imported VM not matched to configured interfaces).
- Provider version: main after v0.119.0

items.title: fix(vm)!: record default tpm_state, efi_disk and amd_sev on import
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Importing a `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` left `tpm_state`, `efi_disk` and `amd_sev` out of state when they used the default settings (TPM on `local-lvm` at `v2.0`, EFI disk on `local-lvm` with default type and format, AMD SEV with default options). Read only recorded these blocks when state already had them or when a value differed from the defaults, and an import starts with empty state. Declaring the existing TPM or EFI disk then planned a new, empty one.

Read now also records these blocks during an import, detected as `vm_id` not yet being in state (the importer sets only the ID and node name). Outside an import the existing rule stays, so configurations that never declared these blocks don't plan their removal.

A CD-ROM on `ide2` has a similar import gap with a different cause; it's tracked separately in #3239.

items.title: vm: refresh fails on stopped VM with qcow2 disks on shared LVM ("volume_size_info ... failed - no format")
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Refreshing a `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` fails when the VM is **stopped** and its disks are **qcow2 on a shared LVM storage** (PVE 9 "snapshot as volume chain"):

```
Error: error get file <storage>:vm-105-disk-0.qcow2 from datastore <storage>: received an HTTP 500 response - Reason: volume_size_info on '<storage>:vm-105-disk-0.qcow2' failed - no format
```

When the VM is stopped, its LVs are deactivated on every node. When the disk config has no explicit `format=`, the provider looks the format up via the single-volume endpoint (`GET /nodes/{node}/storage/{storage}/content/{volume}`). PVE computes `volume_size_info` for that endpoint, which needs to read the qcow2 header and therefore fails on an inactive LV.

Proxmox partially addressed this in PVE 9.2 (libpve-storage-perl >= 9.1.5, [bug 6819](https://bugzilla.proxmox.com/show_bug.cgi?id=6819)), but **only for the content listing**. The single-volume endpoint still fails by design ("For the exact size, the volume still needs to be activated first").

Confirmed: starting the affected VMs makes the error disappear (their LVs get activated, so the single-volume read succeeds). The failure only occurs while the VM is stopped.

As a result, any plan/apply touching a stopped VM with qcow2-on-LVM disks fails, which blocks CI pipelines.

### To Reproduce

1. Shared LVM storage with `snapshot-as-volume-chain` enabled, PVE 9.2.
2. Create a VM with qcow2 disks on that storage using `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm`.
3. Stop the VM.
4. Run `terraform plan` → error above.

Same behaviour directly on the node:

```console
# Listing works and exposes approximate-size
$ pvesh get /nodes/<node>/storage/<storage>/content --vmid 105
┌────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────┬──────┐
│ format │ volid                                │ approximate-size │ size │ vmid │
╞════════╪══════════════════════════════════════╪══════════════════╪══════╪══════╡
│ qcow2  │ <storage>:vm-105-cloudinit.qcow2     │         8.00 MiB │      │  105 │
│ qcow2  │ <storage>:vm-105-disk-0.qcow2        │         4.00 MiB │      │  105 │
│ qcow2  │ <storage>:vm-105-disk-1.qcow2        │        32.01 GiB │      │  105 │
└────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────┴──────┘

# Single-volume read (what the provider does) fails
$ pvesh get /nodes/<node>/storage/<storage>/content/<storage>:vm-105-disk-0.qcow2
failed to stat '/dev/<vg>/vm-105-disk-0.qcow2'
volume_size_info on '<storage>:vm-105-disk-0.qcow2' failed - no format
```

### Expected behavior

Refreshing a stopped VM with qcow2-on-LVM disks should not fail.

### Root cause in the provider

Only the **format** is used from the response (the size comes from the VM config), in two places:

- `proxmoxtf/resource/vm/disk/disk.go` (`Read`, `if dd.Format == nil` → `GetDatastoreFile`) for regular disks
- `proxmoxtf/resource/vm/vm.go` (`vmReadCustom`, `if vmConfig.EFIDisk.Format == nil` → `GetDatastoreFile`) for the EFI disk

Any error other than `ErrResourceDoesNotExist` is returned as a fatal diagnostic.

### Proposed fix

Infer the format from the volume name before calling the API, as PVE does: file-based storages and qcow2-on-LVM volumes carry the format as extension (`vm-105-disk-0.qcow2`), while block storages (LVM raw, LVM-thin, ZFS, RBD) have no extension and are always raw (and for those, the existing API call works since PVE doesn't need `qemu-img`).

```go
func FormatFromVolumeID(volID string) (string, bool) {
	for _, f := range []string{"qcow2", "raw", "vmdk"} {
		if strings.HasSuffix(volID, "."+f) {
			return f, true
		}
	}
	return "", false
}
```

Use it in both places and only fall back to `GetDatastoreFile` when it returns `false`. This also saves one API call per disk on refresh.

Optional additional fallback: if `GetDatastoreFile` fails, use the content listing filtered by VM ID (`GET .../content?vmid=<id>`), which works on inactive volumes and returns `format`. This would require adding a `vmid` field to `DatastoreFileListRequestBody`.

### Additional context

- Proxmox VE: `pve-manager` 9.2.20, `libpve-storage-perl` 9.1.11
- Provider version: 0.114.0
- Terraform/OpenTofu version: Terraform 1.15.5
- Related upstream bug: https://bugzilla.proxmox.com/show_bug.cgi?id=6819

items.title: Validate that `initialization.interface` does not collide with `disk` or `efi_disk` interfaces
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

When a user assigns the same interface (e.g. `scsi0`) to both a `disk` block and `initialization.interface`, the VM is created without error — PVE accepts all API calls — but ends up in a broken state. Subsequent plans show a perpetual disk diff, and apply fails with the cryptic:

```
Error: Defined disk interface not supported. Interface was , but only [ide sata scsi virtio] are supported
```

See #2182 for a real-world report (closed as user error, but with a note to improve error handling — this issue is that follow-up).

### Describe the solution you'd like

Plan-time validation (`CustomizeDiff` in the SDK resource) that rejects a configuration where `initialization.interface` overlaps with any `disk` or `efi_disk` interface, with a clear message naming the colliding interface. The empty-interface runtime error should also name the offending device instead of printing an empty string.

### Additional context

- The check belongs in the legacy SDK VM resource as a cheap guard, and should also be designed into the Framework VM resource schema validation (#1231)
- Related: #2132 (same symptom, also closed)

items.title: fix(vm): reject initialization interface that collides with disk or efi_disk
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds a plan-time check to the SDK `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` resource. If `initialization.interface` is the same as the interface of a `disk` block, the plan now fails with an error naming both, instead of creating a broken VM.

The check runs in `CustomizeDiff` against the raw config, so it only looks at values set explicitly in the configuration. On create, an unset `initialization.interface` is treated as `ide2`, since that is what the provider uses, so a `disk` on `ide2` is caught too. On update an unset interface is skipped, because the provider detects the existing drive. Unknown values (dynamic blocks, values from other resources) are skipped.

This only covers the plan-time check. The empty interface in the runtime "Defined disk interface not supported" error is not changed here.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

The `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` docs describe `bios` and `efi_disk` as reference entries only; there was no example showing them together, and nothing about the new official arm64 build where guests always boot through UEFI (#3031).

This adds an `Example: UEFI boot` section with a minimal `bios = "ovmf"` + `efi_disk` config, a note on why the EFI disk matters (without it PVE uses a temporary efivars file, so boot entries and Secure Boot state are lost on every stop/start), an admonition for arm64 hosts (`bios = "ovmf"` must still be set explicitly because the provider defaults to `seabios`; `efi_disk.type` is ignored there), and a cross-link from the `efi_disk` reference entry.

items.body:
**Description:**
When creating a VM with the `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` resource, Terraform repeatedly tries to update the disk configuration even though no changes were made in the configuration.

**Terraform configuration (simplified):**

```hcl
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm" {
  count = var.size

  name        = "${var.vms_name}-${count.index}"
  description = var.description
  tags        = var.tags

  node_name = var.node
  pool_id   = proxmox_virtual_environment_pool.pool.id

  bios = "ovmf"

  agent {
    enabled = var.agent_on
  }

  cpu {
    sockets      = 1
    limit        = 4
    cores        = var.resources.cpu
    architecture = var.base.arch
  }

  memory {
    dedicated = var.resources.memory * 1024
    floating  = 0
    hugepages = var.resources.hugepg ? "any" : null
  }

  network_device {
    bridge = "vmbr0"
  }

  initialization {
    datastore_id = var.disks.cloudinit.storage
    interface    = "scsi0"

    ip_config {
      ipv4 {
        address = "${cidrhost(var.network.cidr, count.index + 2)}/${local.mask_part}"
        gateway = cidrhost(var.network.cidr, 1)
      }
    }

    user_data_file_id = proxmox_virtual_environment_file.cloudinit_pve[count.index].id
  }

  disk {
    import_from = proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file.cloudinit_img.id
    interface   = "virtio0"
    size        = var.disks.root.size
    discard     = "on"
    iothread    = true

    datastore_id = var.disks.root.storage
  }

  efi_disk {
    datastore_id = "SSD"
    type = "4m"
  }

  dynamic "disk" {
    for_each = { for i, disk in var.disks.other: i => disk }

    content {
      interface    = "scsi${disk.key}"
      size         = disk.value.size
      datastore_id = disk.value.storage
    }
  }
}
```

**Observed behavior (`terraform plan`):**
Terraform reports an in-place update for an existing VM due to a `disk` block, even when nothing changed in configuration:

```
  ~ disk {
      + aio          = "io_uring"
      + backup       = true
      + cache        = "none"
      + datastore_id = "SSD"
      + discard      = "ignore"
      + interface    = "scsi0"
      + iothread     = false
      + replicate    = true
      + size         = 32
      + ssd          = false
    }
```

**Error when applying (`terraform apply`):**

```
Error: Defined disk interface not supported. Interface was , but only [ide sata scsi virtio] are supported

  with module.master_pool.proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.vm[1],
  on modules/pve_pool/main.tf line 97, in resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm":
  97: resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm":
```

**Expected behavior:**

* Terraform should recognize the disk as already in the desired state and not attempt to update it unnecessarily.
* If an update is required, the provider should handle the `interface` field correctly instead of treating it as an empty string.

**Additional notes:**

* This issue occurs with both the root disk and dynamically attached disks.
* Seems like a diff bug where provider-generated defaults (`aio`, `backup`, `cache`, etc.) are not normalized against the configuration.
* Might also be related to the way `discard` is handled (`ignore` vs `on`).

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Define a VM with a root disk and optional dynamic disks as shown above.
2. Run `terraform apply` to create the VM.
3. Run `terraform plan` again without making changes.
4. Observe Terraform trying to modify the disk and failing with the error above.

### What does this PR do?

Phase 1, PR #2 of the [#1231](https://github.com/bpg/terraform-provider-proxmox/issues/1231) epic (migrate `proxmox_vm` to Plugin Framework). Doc-only.

Adds **ADR-008: Sub-block Contract** — codifies the existing Value-centric pattern shared by the five `fwprovider/nodes/vm/` sub-packages (`cpu`, `vga`, `rng`, `cdrom`, `memory`) so the next wave of sub-packages (`disk`, `network_device`, `usb`, `hostpci`, `numa`, `serial_device`, `parallel`, `virtiofs`, `audio_device`, `efi_disk`, `tpm_state`, `agent`, `watchdog`, `amd_sev`, `initialization`, `operating_system`, `smbios`, `startup`) can be ported uniformly. Documents both signature families (single-nested and map-keyed), the `NewValue` null-Object rule with the cores/sockets carve-out, the single-vs-map decision rule with PVE source-bound slot regexes, and the "block name = single PVE concept" rule that retires the legacy `cpu.numa` / `cpu.hotplugged` misnomers.

items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

If we deploy a VM, with guest-agent enabled cloud-image, and set `reboot=true` then the reboot command hangs with `qmp command 'guest-ping' failed - got timeout` and the VM is never rebooted due to proxmox issuing `guest-ping` command before the guest-agent service loads up in it.

nixos cloud-images support guest-agent but it takes some time to start the service.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Adding a 15-second delay to `reboot` command fixes this issues as qemu-guest-agent service is up when vm is booted. then the reboot command is issued to the VM and is successful.

**Additional context**

I've tested this with nixos cloud-image VM's and it works.  Below patch works for me.

https://github.com/HritwikSinghal/terraform-provider-proxmox/commit/de7d523fdd857e1821805a53ed3cbe615fa5250a

Can we fix this by adding a `reboot_delay` param?

items.title: fix(vm): use move_disk API for EFI disk and TPM state storage migration
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes EFI disk storage migration (changing `datastore_id`) which previously either errored with "resizing not supported" or silently recreated the disk (losing UEFI variable data) instead of properly moving it.

Four bugs in the SDK provider's disk change planning caused this:

1. **Nesting bug** — EFI disk and TPM state change detection was nested inside the regular disk change check, so EFI-only storage changes were never processed for `move_disk`.
2. **Pointer comparison** — The resize guard compared `*DiskSize` pointers (memory addresses) instead of dereferenced values, incorrectly triggering "resizing not supported" when regular disks also changed.
3. **Hardcoded DatastoreID** — `vmGetEfiDiskAsStorageDevice` set DatastoreID to `"0"` instead of extracting it from the FileVolume, so the datastore comparison never detected a change.
4. **Config PUT instead of move_disk** — The provider sent a config update (creating a new empty disk) instead of using the `move_disk` API (which preserves data).

The same bugs existed in the TPM state code path and are fixed preventatively.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes perpetual plan drift for physical disk passthrough (`datastore_id = ""` with `path_in_datastore` set). The disk `size` attribute was `Optional + Default(8)` without `Computed`, so Terraform re-applied the default on every plan instead of preserving the actual device size from state. This produced a `size = 7452 -> 8` diff on every run and errored on apply with "Cannot shrink ... not supported!"

The fix adds `Computed: true` to `size` (using `DefaultFunc` instead of `Default`, since SDK v2 disallows `Default + Computed`). For new resources, the default of 8 GB is preserved. For existing resources, the state value (actual device size from API) is used, eliminating drift.

Fixes an issue where adding an `efi_disk` block to an existing VM with OVMF BIOS forced VM replacement. The `type` attribute had `ForceNew: true`, so Terraform saw it transition from empty to `"2m"` (the default) and planned a destroy+create — even though no actual type change was occurring.

items.title: fix(ssh): harden try_sudo for PVE 9, improve shell compatibility
items.body:
## fix(ssh,disk): harden try_sudo command execution for PVE 9 non-interactive shells

### Summary

This PR fixes multiple shell command execution issues affecting **custom disk creation and file uploads on Proxmox VE 9**, while remaining fully backward-compatible with Proxmox VE 8.

The issues were caused by incorrect shell argument handling combined with stricter behavior of non-interactive SSH shells in PVE 9.

---

### Problem Description

On Proxmox VE 9, several SSH-based operations (notably custom disk creation via `file_id` and `NodeStreamUpload`) failed with errors such as:

- `No such file or directory`
- `pvesm path <storage>:<file> not found`
- `unexpected EOF while looking for matching '"'`

Although the same workflows worked on PVE 8, PVE 9 exposes latent bugs due to:

- stricter shell parsing
- reduced default `PATH` in non-interactive SSH sessions
- incorrect argument forwarding in helper shell functions

---

### Root Causes

1. **Incorrect `try_sudo` implementation**  
   The helper function used `$1` instead of `"$@"`, breaking any command with multiple arguments.

2. **Invalid `try_sudo` call pattern**  
   Some call sites passed entire commands as a single quoted string (e.g. `try_sudo "cmd arg1 arg2"`), which is not compatible with proper shell argument handling.

3. **Quoting issues in `bash -c` execution**  
   Commands containing double quotes were injected into a single-quoted `bash -c` context, leading to parsing errors (`unexpected EOF`).

4. **Stricter non-interactive shell environment in PVE 9**  
   The default PATH no longer reliably includes `/sbin` or `/usr/sbin`.

---

### Changes Introduced

- Fixed `try_sudo` to correctly forward arguments using `"$@"`
- Updated all `try_sudo` call sites to pass commands and arguments separately
- Removed unsafe double-quoted command strings from injected shell scripts
- Ensured consistent, POSIX-safe shell execution in non-interactive SSH sessions
- No schema, API, or behavior changes outside SSH execution paths

---

- [x] Proxmox VE 9: custom disk creation and file uploads now work reliably

- [x] No provider configuration changes required
